neutral_facts.value: The prosecution case was that the accused poured acid on the victim, causing extensive burn injuries. The victim died one day after the incident. The FIR was initially registered under Section 326 IPC, but the case was later altered to Section 302 IPC after the victim's death. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 302 IPC and sentenced him to life imprisonment. The High Court affirmed the conviction. The accused was apprehended by witnesses who were present at the scene and who witnessed the act of pouring acid on the victim. The victim's statement, recorded under Section 161 CrPC, was considered a dying declaration and was relied upon by the prosecution. The recovery memo disclosed the recovery of rubber gloves used by the accused during the incident. The victim's statement was recorded shortly after the incident, and he was sent to the hospital for treatment. The medical report indicated that the victim was conscious for at least half an hour after the attack. The accused was not injured during the incident, which was noted as not affecting the prosecution case.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution case was that PWs 1 and 3 saw the accused-appellant sprinkling acid on the body of 'Y' who suffered extensive burn injuries. FIR was registered against the appellant under Section 326 IPC. PW-4 recorded the statement of 'Y' under Section 161 CrPC. 'Y' died one day after the incident. Thereafter the case was altered to that under Section 302 IPC. The trial Court convicted the appellant under Section 302, IPC and sentenced him to life imprisonment.

FIR was registered against the appellant under Section 326 IPC. PW-4 recorded the statement of 'Y' under Section 161 CrPC. 'Y' died one day after the incident. Thereafter the case was altered to that under Section 302 IPC. The trial Court convicted the appellant under Section 302, IPC and sentenced him to life imprisonment.

defence_argument.value: The substantial contention made on behalf of the appellant was that PW1 and 3 could not have witnessed the incident and that having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased 'Y', he could not have made a statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. It was further contended on behalf of the appellant that even if the statement can be said to have been made by the deceased, the same cannot be treated as a dying declaration for non-fulfillment of the statutory requirements and that absence of the acid marks on the accused belied the case of the prosecution. One other submission made on behalf of the appellant was that PWs -1 and 3 were stock witnesses and, therefore, their version could not have been relied upon.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Court applied the principle that a statement made by a person who is dead or cannot be found is relevant under Section 32(1) of the Evidence Act, and that such a statement can be treated as a dying declaration even if it was recorded under Section 161 CrPC, provided it meets the criteria of a dying declaration.
